title: Paint order follows DOM order and ignores CSS stacking (z-index, positioned vs in-flow). Absolute badges, tooltips and overlays end up hidden
evidence: layout-grid-stacking: the 'Guest favorite' and '-20%' badges ( placed BEFORE the ) are visible in orig.png but missing in render.png. The tree lists span.absolute ABS as the first child of article, before 'img · 1'. layout-zorder-transforms: the tooltip (absolute z-20, first in DOM) disappears behind the aside. The hero '-z-10' gradient (last in DOM) is painted OVER the title and toggle, giving a gray wash. layout-grid-stacking: the fuchsia blur blob (absolute, last) is placed after the z-10 content.
rootCause: ui.html childrenOf()/walk() emit children strictly in DOM order, and nothing reorders them. In CSS, positioned descendants paint after in-flow non-positioned ones, and z-index orders them further. Figma paints strictly by layer order, ABSOLUTE children of Auto Layout frames included.
verifierNotes:
I re-ran both cases and confirmed the bug.

- **layout-grid-stacking** (diff 63.5%): orig.png shows the "Guest favorite" and "-20%" pills on the first two card images. render.png has neither, because the image paints over them. The "-20%" span has no z-index at all. It is above the image only because CSS paints positioned elements after in-flow ones, so z-index alone does not explain this case.
- **layout-zorder-transforms** (diff 10.2%): the hero's `-z-10` gradient comes last in the DOM and is painted over the title and the Monthly/Yearly toggle, giving the gray wash. The `z-20` tooltip comes before the aside in the DOM and is completely hidden behind it.

Root cause, confirmed in ui.html:
- `childrenOf()` pushes `walk()` results strictly in DOM order, and `extract()` does the same for the page root.
- Nothing in `walk()`, `frameNode()` or `tryAutoLayout()` reorders children.
- `code.js` `buildNode()` appends children in array order, and `dev/render.html` builds them in the same order.

So this is a real plugin bug, not a renderer artifact. Real Figma paints by layer order too, including ABSOLUTE children of Auto Layout frames.

Problems with the proposed fix:
1. **It misses cases where CSS honors z-index or treats an element as positioned.**
   - z-index also applies to flex and grid items that are not positioned (Tailwind `z-10` on a flex child without `relative`).
   - Elements with `opacity<1`, a transform, filter or `isolation:isolate` but `position:static` paint in the positioned z:auto layer.
   - Chrome's computed zIndex returns the specified value even for static elements, so the check needs a guard.
2. **Sorting in-flow kids before `tryAutoLayout()` breaks Auto Layout detection.** `fitLayout()` requires the array order to match the geometric main-axis order. The `relative z-10 scale-105` Pro pricing card (bucket 3) would move to the end of its row, its gaps would go negative, and the row would lose Auto Layout. The fix must keep the relative order of in-flow kids whenever Auto Layout is detected. This is safe: `fitLayout()` only accepts kids that don't overlap (gap >= -1.5), so their relative paint order cannot matter.
3. **It doesn't say what happens when walk() lifts a wrapper's children.** The `plain && kids.length===1` case, collapsed 0x0 wrappers and `display:contents` all do this, so the key must be propagated.
4. **The optional "hoist" step is risky and should be dropped for now.** Hoisting a descendant to a parent level changes its coordinate space, escapes the intermediate frame's clipping, and conflicts with Auto Layout. All observed failures are fixed at sibling level.

`itemReverseZIndex` does exist in the Figma API, but it is unnecessary for the corrected algorithm.

Known remaining approximations, rare in practice:
- A negative-z child whose parent is not a stacking context should paint below the parent's own background. In Figma it will still paint above the parent's fills. Tailwind usually adds `isolate` or `relative` to the parent, so this seldom shows.
- Positive-z descendants inside non-stacking-context siblings are not hoisted.

title: Any unequal vertical gap (margins between stacked blocks) drops the whole container, often the ROOT page frame, to absolute positioning
evidence: layout-flex-variants: the root frame has no layout because the section gaps are 0,0,12,0,0. section.hero (eyebrow mb-12, h1 mb-20, lead mb-36) has no layout. div.plan (button with mt-auto) has no layout. layout-mobile-app: div.app and div.card have no layout. layout-legacy-structures: main has no layout (crumbs, h2, p and the kpis use different margins), and so do the div.kpi cards (gaps 5 and 1). layout-grid-stacking: the hero text column has no layout. In Figma, editing a heading would not push anything below it on these pages.
rootCause: ui.html fitLayout(): `if (gaps.some((g) => Math.abs(g - gap) > T)) return null;` requires all gaps to be equal, and tryAutoLayout() has no fallback.
fix:
In ui.html, change fitLayout(frame, kids, dir, spaceBetween, allowUneven) so that when allowUneven is true it skips the gap-equality check and returns the layout with `gaps` attached (l._gaps = gaps). Every other check stays as it is: no overlaps (g >= -T), start/end >= -T, and the cross-axis alignment test across ALL kids.

In tryAutoLayout(frame, cs), after the existing strict loop over dirs fails, add a fallback:

1. Choose the axis. dir = the flex direction when cs.display is flex. Otherwise dir = 'VERTICAL' only; never do this on the HORIZONTAL fallback of a block container. Grid containers already fail on overlaps.

2. Get the relaxed fit: `l = fitLayout(frame, kids, dir, false, true)`. If it returns null, stop.

3. Push-to-end special case (mt-auto or justify-between in cards). Let gmax be the largest gap and gnext the second largest. If gmax is the LAST gap, gmax > 2*gnext + 8, and the frame's height is not hugging (the frame is a stretched card or has a fixed height), do this: wrap kids[0..n-2] (recursively, as in step 4) into one group G, then set the frame's layout to SPACE_BETWEEN with children [G, last], spacing 0 and primarySizing 'FIXED'. Mirror this when the FIRST gap is the outlier.

4. General case, agglomerative grouping, which must be deterministic.
   - items = kids. Repeat while the distinct gap values (clustered within ±T) number more than 1, for at most 4 levels:
     - m = min(gaps).
     - For each maximal run of ≥2 consecutive items joined by gaps within m±T, replace the run with a synthetic group node:
       - The node is `{ type:'FRAME', name: groupName(run), fills:[], clip:false, children: run }`.
       - Main axis: pos = pos(run[0]), len = end(run.at(-1)) - pos(run[0]).
       - Cross axis: the PARENT'S INNER cross extent, i.e. x = l.pl and w = frame.w - l.pl - l.pr for VERTICAL, not the bbox of the kids.
       - Rebase every child: child.x -= g.x and child.y -= g.y.
       - g.layout = { mode: dir, spacing: r2(m), primaryAlign:'MIN', counterAlign: l.counterAlign, primarySizing: dir==='VERTICAL' ? 'AUTO' : 'FIXED', padding 0 }.
       - g.stretch = true. Call markStretch(g, g.children, g.layout).
     - Recompute the gaps between the new items.
   - When one gap value remains, set frame.layout with spacing equal to that value and the start/end padding taken from l.
   - Fallback when 4 levels are not enough: build a flat layout with spacing 0 and insert transparent spacer frames between the items, `{type:'FRAME', name:'spacer', fills:[], w: crossInner, h: gap, stretch:true}` for VERTICAL. Skip a spacer where gap <= T.

5. Safety:
   - Only group runs that are contiguous in frame.children. If an absolute child sits between two members in the children array, end the run there to keep paint order. Insert each group at the array index of its first member.
   - Never create a group with a single child.
   - Never group when the frame has fewer than 3 in-flow kids. With 2 kids the gaps are trivially equal.
   - Name groups after the first heading or TEXT inside: `(firstText || 'Group')`, truncated to 24 characters.
   - Call markStretch(frame, newItems, frame.layout) at the end.

Expected results: the hero [eyebrow,h1]@10 → [G,lead]@17 → [G,cta]@37. The landing root becomes a group of 4 sections @0 plus the footer @96. The pricing card becomes [Group(title,price,list), button] with SPACE_BETWEEN. legacy main gets spacers if it does not converge.

code.js needs no change. It already builds a FRAME with fills [] and layout, and handles stretch and the AUTO hug after its children are built.
verifierNotes:
I confirmed this in the code and in the harness. In ui.html, fitLayout() returns null whenever any gap differs from the mean by more than T=1.5, via `if (gaps.some((g) => Math.abs(g - gap) > T)) return null;`. tryAutoLayout() then has no fallback, so the frame keeps absolute positions.

I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs layout-flex-variants` and `landing`, then walked the JSON trees to list in-flow frames with no layout:
- layout-flex-variants: the root frame (vgaps 0,0,12,0,0), section.hero (10,17,37) and all three div.plan cards (8,16,78 / 8,16,24 / 8,16,51, where the button is pushed down by mt-auto).
- The baseline landing.json case has the same problem. Its root page frame has vgaps 0,0,0,96 (the footer margin), its section.hero has 19,11,33, and each div.card has 18,7.
- layout-mobile-app: div.app (8,0,0,0,16) and div.card (6,18).
- layout-legacy-structures: main (8,4,24,28,16,28,28,28).

So the gap is real and appears on nearly every page, including the existing baseline case, usually at the root. The cause is the plugin, not a renderer artifact. Pixels stay correct (diffPct 0.77 and 1.02, because absolute positions reproduce the layout exactly), so this is an editability problem: in Figma, editing a heading does not push the content below it. That is why I rate it medium rather than high ("visibly broken").

The proposed fix (grouping by proximity at the minimum gap, plus a SPACE_BETWEEN special case for mt-auto) is the right direction, but it is under-specified in ways that would cause bugs or no gain:
(a) A depth cap of 3 often does not converge. main in legacy-structures has 5 distinct gap values, and the proposal then has no fallback, so nothing improves.
(b) It does not say how to size and rebase the groups. Wrong cross sizes break STRETCH and responsiveness.
(c) It would also run on the HORIZONTAL fallback for non-flex blocks, and it ignores absolute siblings between grouped kids, which changes z-order.
(d) "Fails ONLY on gap equality" requires fitLayout to report why it failed.

I am confident in all the Figma APIs involved: frames with fills=[], primaryAxisSizingMode AUTO, layoutAlign STRETCH and primaryAxisAlignItems SPACE_BETWEEN.

title: Auto Layout padding and alignment are inferred from leftover space instead of CSS padding and justify/align, so frames get huge fake paddings and wrong hug or fixed sizing
evidence: layout-flex-variants: cta-row (justify-content:center) gets pa=MIN pl=402.68 pr=402.67. demo.end gets pl=799. space-around/evenly become MIN with spacing 288.71 or 156.46 and padding 161. layout-legacy-structures: aside (CSS padding 24) gets pb=703 while hugging (ps=AUTO), so adding a nav item would grow it past 900. layout-zorder-transforms: the chart (p-6) gets pt=32.81 inferred from the tallest bar, which is then also marked STRETCH. Pricing cards stretched by the row get pb=25 instead of 1. layout-mobile-app tabbar: the 'Stats' tab gets ca=MIN because its icon is only 1.09px off-center (< T=1.5), while the other tabs are CENTER.
rootCause: ui.html fitLayout() computes pl/pr/pt/pb from the measured first and last child positions and only uses CENTER for a single child. The CSS paddings, border widths, justify-content and align-items available in tryAutoLayout() via cs are ignored, except for space-between. primarySizing 'AUTO' is set for every vertical frame regardless of whether its height is content-determined.
fix:
Changes are in ui.html, in tryAutoLayout(), fitLayout() and markStretch(), plus small additions in code.js place().

1. Give fitLayout the CSS values and the children's margins.
- When building child layer nodes in the walker, attach each child's computed margins as a non-enumerable property, so postMessage drops it: `Object.defineProperty(node, '_m', { value: { t, r, b, l }, enumerable: false })`. A WeakMap from layer node to element also works.
- In tryAutoLayout, compute the inner insets of the frame itself: `P = { t: pt + bt, r: pr + br, b: pb + bb, l: pl + bl }`, taken from cs padding and border widths. Keep strokesIncludedInLayout at its default (false). The INSIDE stroke is drawn over the border area, so padding + border reproduces CSS border-box exactly. Do not add the border to padding and also set strokesIncludedInLayout.
- Call fitLayout(frame, kids, dir, { flex, jc: cs.justifyContent, ai: cs.alignItems, P }).

2. Main axis. Keep the existing DOM-order and equal-gap checks. Let Ps/Pe be the start and end insets on the main axis (l/r or t/b). Let mS = the first child's leading margin and mE = the last child's trailing margin on that axis. Compute the measured `start` and `end` as today, then `ls = start - Ps` and `le = end - Pe`.
- If `-T <= ls <= mS + T`: start is explained by padding plus the first child's margin (which may have collapsed).
- If `-T <= le <= mE + T`: end is explained by padding plus the last child's margin.
Then decide, in this order:
- (a) Start explained, end not, and jc is not end, flex-end, center or space-*: MIN. pStart = start, pEnd = Pe.
- (b) End explained, start not (jc end or flex-end, or a non-flex frame whose children sit at the end): MAX. pStart = Ps, pEnd = end.
- (c) `|ls - le| <= T` and ls > T: CENTER. pStart = Ps, pEnd = Pe, spacing = gap. This works for n > 1 too.
- (d) flex, jc space-around or space-evenly, n >= 2, ls > T and le > T: SPACE_BETWEEN with pStart = start and pEnd = end, the measured values. This is exact because Figma's (inner - sum) / (n - 1) equals the measured gap. If n == 1, use CENTER.
- (e) flex and jc space-between: SPACE_BETWEEN, as today.
- (f) Both ends explained: MIN with pStart = start, pEnd = end.
- (g) Otherwise, fall back to the current behaviour: MIN with the measured start and end.
For a non-flex frame the jc tests do not apply; use only the geometric conditions.

3. Cross axis. Let Pa and Pb be the cross insets, `before'[i] = before[i] - Pa` and `after'[i] = after[i] - Pb`.
- Test CENTER as `same(before' - after')` against the inner box, and test it FIRST when the frame is flex with ai = center.
- For ai = flex-end or end, test `same(after')` first.
- For ai = baseline on a HORIZONTAL frame, emit 'BASELINE' (Figma and the mock accept it) only when the geometric test is inconclusive. Otherwise keep the geometric result.
- For MIN, set the cross padding to Pa and Pb, not min(after). For MAX, set Pa and Pb. For CENTER, set Pa and Pb.
- If the children do not fit the inner box (before' or after' < -T, e.g. negative margins), fall back to the current floor0 values.
- Do not try to map per-child align-self values other than stretch.

4. Sizing.
- `primarySizing = 'AUTO'` only when the frame is VERTICAL, the end is explained (step 2), and primary is not SPACE_BETWEEN or MAX/CENTER with real slack. In other words, the height is content-defined. Otherwise use FIXED.
- markStretch then marks such a FIXED column as STRETCH in a row whose align-items is stretch, because its existing guard only skips AUTO columns. This fixes the aside: pb = 24, FIXED height, STRETCH in the row.
- For a child with computed flex-grow > 0 inside a flex parent that got auto layout, set `k.grow = 1`. In code.js place(), in the `auto` branch, add `if (n.grow) node.layoutGrow = 1;`. This is valid only for children of an auto-layout parent. Mirror it in dev/render.html (flex-grow: 1) if needed.

5. Regression guard. Every branch reproduces the measured child positions exactly, so the import geometry does not change. Re-run all dev/cases. diffPct and heightDelta should stay the same or improve, with 0 mockErrors. Spot-check the JSON:
- cta-row: CENTER, pl/pr 0.
- flex-end demo: MAX, pl 16.
- space-around tab bar: SPACE_BETWEEN.
- 'Stats' tab: CENTER.
- aside: pb 24, FIXED.
verifierNotes:
I confirmed this by reading the code and re-running the harness. In ui.html, tryAutoLayout() passes only `spaceBetween` to fitLayout(). fitLayout() then sets the main-axis padding from the measured first and last child offsets (`start`, `end`) and the cross-axis padding from `floor0(before/after)`. It uses CENTER only when there is exactly one child. It sets `primarySizing = !H && primary !== 'SPACE_BETWEEN' ? 'AUTO' : 'FIXED'`, so every vertical frame hugs. CSS padding, border, justify-content and align-items are never read.

I re-ran the cases on the current code:
- layout-flex-variants: diff 3.01%, 0 mock errors.
- layout-legacy-structures: diff 1.25%, 0 mock errors.

The JSON trees show what the other agent reported:
- `div.cta-row` (justify-content:center): MIN with pl 402.22 and pr 402.21.
- The flex-end demo: MIN with pl 799.67.
- The space-around and space-evenly demos: MIN with spacing 289.16 or 156.54 and padding 161 or 173.
- `ul`s inside a card: fake right padding of about 130 to 141.
- `nav.crumbs` and `toolbar`: pr 980 and 898.
- `aside`: VERTICAL, ps=AUTO, pb=709.56. It hugs, so its height is content plus 709. Adding a nav item makes it grow past the row.
- layout-mobile-app tabbar (space-around): MIN with spacing 329.71 and padding 164.87 at 1440 px, 67.21 and 33.6 at 390 px.
- The 'Stats' `a.tab` gets ca=MIN while its siblings get CENTER. The cause is that `same(before)` (T=1.5) is tested before the centering test, so a 1.09 px offset reads as start-aligned.

Severity: the pixel diff barely shows this, because every frame is fixed-size or its fake padding reproduces the measured box exactly. Right after import the result looks correct. It breaks when the user edits the layers: text in a centered or end-aligned row stays left-anchored, a space-around tab bar cannot rebalance, and a stretched sidebar grows instead of keeping its height. That is noticeable on many AI-generated pages but not visibly broken at import, so I rate it medium rather than high.

Flaws in the proposed fix:
1. It adds the border widths to padding and also sets strokesIncludedInLayout = true. That counts the border twice, because Figma then lays children out inside both the stroke and the padding. Use only one of the two. The safer option is padding = CSS padding + border, with the stroke left out of layout (the default, already INSIDE). It also avoids depending on an API property the mock does not model.
2. It replaces geometry with CSS justify and align. The CSS value has to stay a hint, checked against the measured positions. Without that check, margin:auto, flex-grow, overflowing content, collapsed margins and inline-flex wrappers would produce frames that differ from the browser.
3. The free-space test `|F| ≤ T` ignores child margins. A block or column whose last child has margin-bottom has F > 0 but a content-defined height. The proposal would wrongly switch it to FIXED.
4. "padding += gap" for space-evenly and space-around is ambiguous. It must use the free-space slot, not the CSS gap. The measured leading offset already equals P + slot, so use the measured start and end directly.
5. Per-child alignSelf cannot be mapped. Figma's layoutAlign MIN, CENTER and MAX are deprecated no-ops. Mixed alignment has to keep the current geometric path.
6. Baseline only exists for HORIZONTAL frames (counterAxisAlignItems 'BASELINE'). Otherwise use the geometric test.

title: flex-wrap rows and CSS grid card grids never get Auto Layout
evidence: layout-flex-variants: div.tags (flex-wrap, 2 lines) has no layout and 9 absolute chips. layout-grid-stacking: div.grid (3-col card grid, 5 cards) has no layout, and so does the bento grid (grid-cols-4 with col-span-2/row-span-2). layout-legacy-structures: dl (grid 160px 1fr) has no layout, and kpis only works because auto-fit happened to fit in one row. At 390 the 1-col card grid does become V layout.
rootCause: ui.html tryAutoLayout()/fitLayout() only try a single-line HORIZONTAL or VERTICAL layout. Wrapped lines produce negative main-axis gaps, so the fit returns null. layoutWrap and grid are never considered.
fix:
ui.html, tryAutoLayout(frame, cs): keep the current single-line attempt first. If it returns null and either (cs.display is flex, flexDirection is row and flexWrap is not 'nowrap') or (display is grid), call a new fitWrap(frame, kids, cs). If that also fails and display is grid, call fitGrid(frame, kids, cs).

fitWrap(frame, kids, cs), with T = 1.5:
1. Build lines in DOM order. Start a new line when k.y >= prevLineTop + T and k.x < prev.x + prev.w - T. Reject (return null) if any line's top is not strictly greater than the previous line's top, if x is not increasing inside a line, or if fewer than 2 lines result.
2. For each line, gaps = x[i] - (x[i-1] + w[i-1]). All gaps across all lines must equal one value colGap within T (cs.columnGap in px is a cross-check). A one-item line has no gaps.
3. Padding: pl = min over lines of the first item's x. lineBottom = max(y + h) over the line. rowGaps = nextLine.top - prevLine.bottom must all match within T: that value is rowGap. pt = first line's top, pb = frame.h - last line's bottom. Reject if any value is below -T.
4. Per-line main alignment. MIN: every line starts at pl. CENTER: start and end slack are equal on every line. SPACE_BETWEEN: each multi-item line touches both edges; keep the last line MIN only if Figma would put it there, otherwise reject. Map justify-content to these; anything else rejects.
5. Cross alignment within each line: compare item tops with lineTop, item bottoms with lineBottom, or centers. Give MIN, MAX or CENTER, using the existing same() logic per line.
6. Line-break reproduction, the critical step. Let inner = frame.w - pl - pr and lineW = sum(w) + colGap*(n-1). Require lineW <= inner + 0.01 on every line. For every line except the last, require lineW + colGap + w(first item of next line) > inner + 0.01. If that fails and the alignment is MIN, shrink the box: set pr = frame.w - pl - maxLineW - 0.01 (it must be >= 0), then re-check. Otherwise reject. Round child widths with r2 before summing, so float error can't cause an early wrap in Figma.
7. Return { mode:'HORIZONTAL', wrap:true, spacing: r2(colGap), counterSpacing: r2(rowGap), primaryAlign, counterAlign, primarySizing:'FIXED', pt, pr, pb, pl }.

markStretch: return early when l.wrap is set. Wrapped children keep FIXED width and height.

code.js applyLayout(node, n), ES2017: after node.layoutMode = l.mode, add `if (l.wrap && 'layoutWrap' in node) { node.layoutWrap = 'WRAP'; node.counterAxisSpacing = l.counterSpacing; node.counterAxisAlignContent = 'AUTO'; }`. If the 'layoutWrap' in node check fails, applyLayout should treat the frame as having no layout: skip setting layoutMode, so children are placed by x/y. Do this by checking at the top of applyLayout and having place() see layoutMode 'NONE'.

fitGrid, only for grids that wrap can't express (row or column spans, as in the bento):
1. Parse cs.gridTemplateColumns and cs.gridTemplateRows. Computed values are px lists; reject on 'none', 'subgrid' or `[line names]`.
2. Compute track start offsets using cs.columnGap/cs.rowGap and the content-box origin (padding + border).
3. Map each kid's measured box to colStart/colEnd/rowStart/rowEnd by matching its edges to track edges within T. Reject on any mismatch, or if two kids overlap.
4. Emit { mode:'GRID', cols:[px...], rows:[px...], colGap, rowGap, cells:[{r, c, rs, cs}], padding }.

In code.js, only when 'gridRowCount' in node:
1. node.layoutMode = 'GRID'; set gridColumnCount and gridRowCount; set gridColumnGap and gridRowGap; set gridColumnSizes and gridRowSizes to arrays of { type:'FIXED', value:px }; set the paddings.
2. After all children are appended, for each child: child.setGridChildPosition(r, c), then child.gridColumnSpan = cs and child.gridRowSpan = rs.
3. Wrap the whole block in try/catch. On any error, set node.layoutMode = 'NONE' and reassign every child's x/y from the tree.
4. Without the API, or when fitGrid rejects, keep absolute positioning as today. Do not add synthetic row frames.

Harness: dev/mock-figma.js and dev/render.html must learn layoutWrap, counterAxisSpacing and counterAxisAlignContent (and GRID, if implemented). Until then the new layouts can't be validated, and the strict mock may reject them.
verifierNotes:
I re-ran the harness. layout-grid-stacking gives diff 2.81%, 33 auto layouts. layout-flex-variants first failed with an ENOENT on its temp file, most likely because another agent was running the same case in parallel. On retry it gave diff 0.77%, 51 auto layouts, no mock errors. I then walked the JSON trees:
- flex-variants: div.tags (512x74, 9 chips on 2 lines at y=0 and y=42) has layout '-'.
- grid-stacking: div.grid (1104x588, 5 cards of 352 at x 0/376/752 and y 0/318) has no layout, and neither does the bento div.max-w-6xl, where the row-span-2 item sits next to a second-row item at 584,122.
- legacy-structures: dl (160 + 944 columns, 3 rows) has no layout. div.kpis gets HORIZONTAL only because its 4 items fit on one line.

The code confirms the cause. tryAutoLayout() only tries one direction: flex-direction for flex, or VERTICAL then HORIZONTAL for everything else (grid included). fitLayout() returns null as soon as one main-axis gap is below -T, and a line break always produces one. Nothing reads flexWrap, grid-template or row/column gap, and code.js applyLayout() never sets layoutWrap or counterAxisSpacing. So the gap is real.

Impact: everything is still placed absolutely at the measured positions, so the pixel diff stays low. These pages are not visibly broken. The damage is to editability: the most common AI-page structures (card grids, tag/chip clouds, feature grids, dl lists) arrive as loose absolute layers that don't reflow when edited. That is why I rate it medium, not high.

Problems with the proposed fix:
1. Wrap must not be limited to equal-width grid kids. What matters is that Figma's wrap reproduces the measured line breaks. Without that check it gives wrong results. Example: grid-template-columns: repeat(3,200px) in a 1104px box. Figma would fit 5 items per line, not 3.
2. It must check that DOM order equals visual order. CSS `order`, grid-auto-flow: dense and explicit grid-column/grid-row placement all break that.
3. The "VERTICAL stack of HORIZONTAL row frames" fallback adds frames that aren't in the DOM. It is also redundant, because wrap already covers grids without spans. The dl case also works with plain wrap: 160 + 16 + 944 = 1120 forces 2 items per line.
4. markStretch must skip wrapped kids.
5. GRID mode needs append-then-position ordering and a try/catch fallback.
6. dev/mock-figma.js and dev/render.html know neither layoutWrap nor GRID. They would have to be extended before the harness can validate any of this. I did not edit them, per the rules.

title: CSS transforms (rotate, scale, skew; Tailwind v4 rotate/scale/translate properties) are flattened into the axis-aligned bounding box
evidence: layout-grid-stacking: the hero image with rotate-3 becomes an unrotated RECT [-8,-13.6 544x347] (render shows a straight, bigger card). The 'Summer deals' badge (-rotate-2) is an unrotated 130x28.5 box with fake paddings 4.41/5.43, and its column loses its layout. The FAQ chevron svg rotate-180 points down instead of up. layout-mobile-app: the chevron rotate(-90deg) points down instead of right in every row. layout-zorder-transforms: the rotate-45 diamond becomes a 90x90 square, the skew-x box is a plain rectangle, rotate-90 'SIDE' renders horizontal, and the scale-105 featured card has 1.05× box and padding but unscaled 16px text, which also breaks the pricing row layout (before=-7.8 < -T).
rootCause: ui.html walk() uses getBoundingClientRect(), and textGeometry() uses Range rects, both of which return post-transform axis-aligned boxes. svgNode() clones the SVG without its CSS transform. Nothing reads cs.transform, cs.rotate, cs.scale or cs.translate, and code.js never sets rotation or relativeTransform.
fix:

A simpler check is to compare `rect.width` with the measured max-content width (clone at `width:max-content`, or `el.scrollWidth` for single-line content) within T.

2) After `layout = fitLayout(...)`, compute the CSS insets `cssPad = padding + border` per side:

5. Fixed elements that fill the viewport (inset-0 modals or backdrops) or are centered vertically should keep their scroll-0 position rather than be stretched. Stretching moves their centered content.
6. Sticky headers sit correctly at scroll 0 and need no change.

title: Layer names come from the first CSS class, which on Tailwind pages is a meaningless utility
evidence: Names in the trees: 'div.flex', 'div.relative', 'div.mt-6', 'div.w-full', 'span.rounded-md', 'section.mx-auto', 'nav.hidden', 'div.min-h-screen', 'div.h-12', 'span.w-8', 'div.col-span-2', 'button.rounded-full'. Many frames are just 'div'. In layout-flex-variants the nav button group is 'div', and the 5 cards are all 'article.relative'.
fix:
Change only nameFor(el) in ui.html (pageAgent). Nothing downstream depends on names. Algorithm:
1. label = el.getAttribute('aria-label') || el.getAttribute('data-name') || el.id || el.getAttribute('title'). If set, return `${tag} · ${label}`.
2. role = el.getAttribute('role'). Use it as the base instead of the tag when present (e.g. 'dialog', 'tablist').
3. Pick the first meaningful class, skipping utilities:
   const UTIL = /^(?:!|-)?(?:flex|inline|block|grid|hidden|contents|table|flow-root|static|relative|absolute|fixed|sticky|isolate|container|visible|invisible|collapse|truncate|uppercase|lowercase|capitalize|italic|underline|line-through|antialiased|subpixel-antialiased|sr-only|not-sr-only|group|peer|grow|shrink|transform|transition|d|m[trblxyse]?|p[trblxyse]?|gap|space|w|h|min|max|size|text|font|leading|tracking|bg|from|via|to|border|divide|outline|ring|rounded|shadow|drop|opacity|z|top|left|right|bottom|inset|start|end|items|justify|self|place|content|order|col|row|basis|overflow|overscroll|object|aspect|translate|rotate|scale|skew|origin|duration|ease|delay|animate|cursor|select|pointer|resize|fill|stroke|backdrop|blur|brightness|line|whitespace|break|list|decoration|align|columns|float|clear|mix|filter|scroll|snap|touch|will|accent|caret|appearance)(?:-|$)/;
   const isUtil = (c) => /[:\[\]\/]/.test(c) || UTIL.test(c);
   (Any class with a variant prefix ':', an arbitrary value '[...]' or an opacity '/' is a utility. Otherwise the prefix list decides.)
   cls = classList.find(c => !isUtil(c)).
4. Base: `${role||tag}${cls ? '.'+cls : ''}`.
5. Content hint, only for containers whose base is generic (no meaningful class and tag in div/span/section/article/aside/header/footer/nav/main/li/a/button/label/form/ul/ol): take the hint from the first h1-h6 found with querySelector, or for a/button/label/li use the element itself, otherwise the first descendant text. Compute it as (x.textContent||'').replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim().slice(0,32). If non-empty, return `${base} · ${hint}`. Skip the hint for the page root/body, and for elements with more than ~200 characters of text and no heading (big wrappers), so 'div.min-h-screen' becomes plain 'div' rather than a sentence fragment.
6. Return base.slice(0,60).
Use textContent rather than innerText: it is cheaper and forces no extra layout. Truncate with slice. Results: 'article · Cabin in the woods', 'button · Get started', 'section · Trending stays', 'header', while plain-CSS pages keep 'nav.nav', 'div.card', 'span.chip' unchanged. Do not touch code.js. It already sets node.name = n.name, so the mock and real Figma behave identically.
verifierNotes: Confirmed in ui.html nameFor() (line ~359): after aria-label/id, the name is `${tag}.${firstClass}`, where firstClass is `(el.getAttribute('class')||'').trim().split(/\s+/)[0]`. The existing tree dev/out/tailwind-snippet.json shows exactly that: 'div.min-h-screen', 'header.fixed', 'div.mt-16', 'div.rounded-2xl', 'div.relative', 'span.absolute', 'p.p-4', 'code.bg-slate-100', 'form.grid', 'label.flex', 'pre.bg-slate-900', 'ul.list-disc'. On plain-CSS pages (landing, layout-flex-variants) the names are fine ('nav.nav', 'div.card', 'span.chip'), and a bare 'div' shows up whenever there is no class. So the gap is real, and it hits Tailwind output, which most AI tools produce. Severity: names have no effect on rendering or on the pixel diff, and nothing reads n.name except code.js, which only assigns it (code.js lines 112/117; render.html stores it as a data attribute). So this is cosmetic and affects how editable/navigable the layers panel is, not what the user sees. Under the rubric that makes it low, not medium. Notes on the proposed fix: (1) The part about 'text-wrapper groups created by the gap grouping' is wrong: ui.html has no gap-grouping step that creates synthetic frames. The only FRAME producers are root, frameNode() and boxed() for form controls, and TEXT layers are named by Figma from their characters. (2) The proposed utility regex is incomplete and partly fragile. It misses variant prefixes with hyphens or digits ('group-hover:', '2xl:', '[&>*]:'), the important flag ('!'), arbitrary values ('w-[37px]'), opacity suffixes ('bg-black/50'), logical spacing (ps/pe/ms/me/gap-x), and many standalone utilities: grow, shrink, basis, truncate, uppercase, italic, underline, antialiased, sr-only, group, peer, divide, outline, cursor, select, pointer-events, fill, stroke, backdrop, blur, line-clamp, whitespace, break, list, decoration, animate, transform, origin, table, contents, visible, invisible, static, columns. It also ignores Bootstrap utilities (d-flex, mb-3, col-md-6, text-center). The fix is safe for the real Figma API: it changes only the name strings, and node.name accepts any string. No harness case was needed, because names don't affect pixels and the existing JSON output already shows the problem.

title: Centered max-width containers are expressed as huge parent paddings instead of max-width + centering
evidence: layout-grid-stacking: header.sticky has pad 0,144,1,144 with an inner STRETCH div.max-w-6xl. section.bg-slate-50 has pad 64,144,64,144. layout-flex-variants: footer has pad 25,160,24,160. Resizing the frame to 1280 keeps 144px side paddings, so the container shrinks instead of staying at 1152 centered, which is the opposite of mx-auto behaviour.
rootCause: ui.html fitLayout() turns the centered child's offsets into parent padding (a, b) and marks the child STRETCH.
verifierNotes:
I confirmed this from dev/out/layout-grid-stacking.json, which is newer than ui.html and code.js. header.sticky (w 1440) gets layout {VERTICAL, counterAlign CENTER, pl 144, pr 144} and its only in-flow child, div.max-w-6xl (w 1152), has stretch=true. section.relative and section.bg-slate-50 get the same 144px side paddings. The case source uses `max-w-6xl mx-auto px-6` with no padding on the parents, so in CSS those 144px are auto margins, not padding.

Root cause, ui.html fitLayout(): on the cross axis it turns each kid's measured offset into parent padding. If all kids share the same `before` offset, `a = floor0(before)`, `b = floor0(after)`. For a single kid centered by auto margins, `before == after == 144`, so the parent gets pl = pr = 144. markStretch() then sees `kid.w == frame.w - pl - pr` and sets stretch. In Figma the kid is FILL inside a parent padded by 144. Widen the frame and the container grows past 1152; narrow it and the 144px gutters stay while the content shrinks. That is the opposite of how mx-auto + max-width behaves.

The static snapshot is pixel-identical, so this affects resize behaviour only. Low severity is right. It is a plugin bug, not a renderer artifact.

The proposed fix has the right idea but is underspecified in three places:
- It cannot rely on detecting auto margins from the computed style. getComputedStyle returns resolved px margins, never the word 'auto', so equal left and right gaps are the only signal.
- cs.maxWidth can come back as a percentage or 'none', so only px values qualify.
- markStretch() will no longer mark the kid, because with the parent's real CSS padding the kid is narrower than the inner width. It needs an explicit rule for this case.

Also, neither dev/mock-figma.js nor dev/render.html knows about maxWidth. The renderer applies stretch as align-self:stretch, so after the fix the harness would draw the container 1440 wide and report a false diff. It needs `el.style.maxWidth = n.maxWidth + 'px'` and margin-inline:auto (harness-side follow-up). In real Figma, minWidth/maxWidth exist on auto-layout frames and their direct children, and setting them elsewhere throws, so the write must be guarded. I am fairly confident, but have not checked in this run, that a FILL child clamped by maxWidth gets positioned by the parent's counterAxisAlignItems (CENTER).

title: Floated images: the wrapping paragraph is placed over the float
evidence: layout-legacy-structures: in .note, the img floats left (120x90) and the paragraph becomes TEXT [17,16.8 1086x67] spanning the full width from x=17. In render.png the first lines are drawn on top of the image. orig.png shows them indented around the float.
rootCause: ui.html blockText()/textGeometry() use the full content box as wrapBox, unaware that line boxes next to floats are shorter.
verifierNotes:
I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs layout-legacy-structures` (diffPct 1.25, 0 mock errors) and checked the tree and PNGs myself.

**What the tree shows.** In `div.note` (FRAME 1120x132, layout null), the floated img is RECT [17,17 120x90]. The paragraph is TEXT [17,16.3 1086x67.18] with autoResize HEIGHT.

**What the PNGs show.** I cropped both images to the note:
- `orig.png`: all three lines start at x≈153, which is 17 + 120 + 16 of margin.
- `render.png`: "Analyst note. Revenue…" is drawn over the photo, starting at x=17.

**Not a harness artifact.** Real Figma would draw a 1086-wide text layer over the image in the same way. Line-wrapping also differs: about 950px is available beside the float, versus 1086px in the export.

**Root cause.** In ui.html, `blockText()` calls `textGeometry(el, cs, cb, cb)` with `cb = contentBox(el)`. In the `lines.length > 1` branch, `textGeometry()` returns `x: box.x, w: box.w` from that wrapBox. A non-BFC block next to a float keeps its full-width border box; only its line boxes get shorter. `looseText()` has the same problem.

**Problems with the proposed fix.**
1. It infers the indent from line-rect left edges. That only works for left-aligned text and a left float. With a right float and left-aligned text, the right edges are ragged anyway, so nothing can be detected. With centred or justified text, the rect edges don't show where the line box starts.
2. Option (a), building an explicit HORIZONTAL row, is unnecessary. Once the text no longer overlaps the image, the existing geometry-based Auto Layout detection may produce the row on its own. Building it by hand is wrong when the float ends partway through the paragraph.

**Better approach.** Detect the floats themselves and narrow the wrapBox; details are in the fix field. When the paragraph's own box is already beside the float (it has overflow:hidden, is flow-root, or is a flex item), the inset is no larger than the content box, so nothing changes and existing pages are unaffected. AI-generated pages rarely use float-left text wrapping, so severity stays low.

title: flex align-items: baseline rows (price '$19 /month') are not converted to Auto Layout
evidence: text-inline.json: `div.price` (display:flex; align-items:baseline; gap:10px) with $49 / $19 / '/ month' is a plain FRAME with absolutely placed TEXTs (no layout). The same `flex items-baseline gap-x-1` holds the prices in every Tailwind pricing card (text-tw-pricing).
rootCause: ui.html fitLayout(): cross-axis alignment only tests MIN/MAX/CENTER. Texts of different sizes aligned on the baseline match none of them, so it returns null.
fix:
ui.html only; code.js needs no change because applyLayout already passes counterAlign through.

1) In tryAutoLayout(frame, cs), before the dirs loop, try a baseline layout first:

  if (flex && !/column/.test(cs.flexDirection) && /baseline/.test(cs.alignItems) && !/wrap/.test(cs.flexWrap)) {
    const bl = fitBaselineRow(frame, kids, /space-between/.test(cs.justifyContent));
    if (bl) { frame.layout = bl; markStretch(frame, kids, bl); return; }
  }
  // otherwise fall through to the existing MIN/MAX/CENTER fitLayout (status quo)

2) Add a new function fitBaselineRow(frame, kids, spaceBetween):
  - Gate: every kid is type 'TEXT' with a single line (autoResize 'WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT', or h <= 1.6 * line height). Return null for SVG, RECT or FRAME kids, because Figma's baseline for non-text layers is not reliably the same as CSS's synthesized baseline. Those rows keep today's absolute placement.
  - Main axis: the same checks as fitLayout. Use x in DOM order, gaps >= -T, equal gaps within T=1.5, start and end >= -T. Spacing is the mean gap, or SPACE_BETWEEN with spacing 0 when justify-content is space-between and there is more than one kid.
  - Cross axis: compare line-box tops, not glyph-box tops. For each kid, lh = k.segments[0].lineHeight (px, or null for normal). Then lineTop = lh ? k.y + (k.h - lh) / 2 : k.y. This recovers the real line box when textBox() inflated a line-height:1 text to its content area; for example, Tailwind's $0 goes from y=-4/h=56 to a line top of 0.
  - Set pt = max(0, min(lineTop)) and pb = max(0, frame.h - max(lineTop + (lh || k.h))). Keep the frame's counterAxisSizing FIXED and h unchanged, as applyLayout already does.
  - Optional sanity check: the measured baselines must agree within 1px. Compute baseline_i = glyphTop_i + ascent_i, where glyphTop_i = k.y + (lh ? (k.h - (k.h - lh)) / 2 : 0); it is simpler to record ascent in textBox(). For that, record the range rect's top `T` and use canvas ctx.font = cs.font; ctx.measureText('H').fontBoundingBoxAscent. If the baselines disagree, return null.
  - Return { mode: 'HORIZONTAL', spacing, primaryAlign: spaceBetween ? 'SPACE_BETWEEN' : 'MIN', counterAlign: 'BASELINE', primarySizing: 'FIXED', pl: P(start), pr: P(end), pt: P(pt), pb: P(pb) }.

3) Recommended companion fix in textBox(): stop clamping the half-leading for single-line text: hl = Number.isFinite(lh) ? (lh - rects[0].height) / 2 : 0. Then a line-height:1 TEXT gets y = line-box top and h = lh, which matches the height Figma gives a WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT text with a fixed lineHeight. Today the layer is 56 tall in the tree but 48 in Figma, offset by -4. That is a small existing misplacement in absolute mode too. Keep the clamp for multi-line boxes, or apply the same signed hl there, since Figma also uses negative leading.

Regression safety:
- Only flex rows that declare baseline, contain only TEXT kids and do not wrap are affected.
- Every other row keeps the current logic.
- layout-mobile-app section-h changes from an approximate MAX to an exact BASELINE.

To verify, run node dev/fidelity.mjs text-inline, text-tw-pricing, layout-flex-variants and layout-mobile-app. Confirm that autoLayouts goes up and diffPct stays the same or improves.
verifierNotes:
I re-ran text-inline and text-tw-pricing. The gap is real, but it hurts editability, not how the page looks.

Evidence:
- In text-inline.json, div.price (flex, align-items:baseline) has no `layout`. Its kids are TEXT nodes at y=22/0/25 with h=21/49/17.
- In text-tw-pricing.json, both p.mt-4 (`flex items-baseline`) have no layout either. Their kids are at y=-4 (h=56, lineHeight 48) and y=26.5 (h=20).
- layout-flex-variants div.price has the same problem in all three cards.
- layout-mobile-app section-h (baseline + space-between) only works by luck: it falls back to counterAlign MAX within the 1.5px tolerance.

Root cause is confirmed in ui.html fitLayout(). The cross-axis check accepts only same(before) → MIN, same(after) → MAX, or same(before-after) → CENTER. Baseline-aligned texts of different sizes match none of these, so it returns null. tryAutoLayout() never reads cs.alignItems.

A second cause the original report missed: fitLayout also returns null when any `before` is below -1.5. In the Tailwind case the big price TEXT sits at y=-4. textBox() clamps the half-leading at 0 (`hl = Math.max(0, (lh - rects[0].height)/2)`). So with leading-none (line-height 1), the layer is the 56px glyph content area, not the 48px line box. Skipping only the alignment test would therefore not fix text-tw-pricing.

Visual impact: I cropped the price row from the diff PNG and it has no red pixels. The absolute placement looks correct. The loss is editability. In Figma, changing "$19" to "$199" will not push "/ month" along, and these rows appear in nearly every AI-generated pricing card. That is why I rate it medium, not high.

API check:
- Figma supports counterAxisAlignItems = 'BASELINE', valid only for layoutMode HORIZONTAL.
- mock-figma accepts it, and render.html maps it to align-items: baseline.
- code.js applyLayout passes l.counterAlign through unchanged, so code.js needs no change.

Problems with the proposed fix:
1. It does not handle the negative `before` above, so it would still reject the Tailwind case.
2. Making the baseline check "optional" is unsafe. Figma's baseline rule for non-text children (SVG icons, image RECTs, frames such as badges) is not something I am confident matches CSS's synthesized baseline. The fix must be limited to cases where Figma's result is predictable.
3. pt = min(before) uses glyph-box tops instead of line-box tops, which can put the row's top padding a few px off.

The corrected fix below covers all three. It also must not add BASELINE to flex-wrap rows, because a wrapped row is not one line.
